decisions: Took the sanctioned steps 2-3 split: new corpus + ascension/humility trials frozen, engine withheld to the next session.

Froze corpora/l3streamb (seed 5005, n 10000): the anti-recency-proxy stream — two-tier importance (800 heavy items at 240-260 placed one per stratum on a stratified grid, 9200 light at 1-3), total mass 218418.
Gave l3streamb a shuffled, position-free `tag` as the cue handle, because l3stream's `id = t + 1` makes its cue positionally decodable rather than content-addressed.

Defined the L3 budget as budget_items x event_cost(payload) = 1000 x 11 = 11000 work units on both streams: engine-independent, so an engine pays for its own index, tombstones and cold tier out of the same thousand items.

FINDING: the §5 L3 gate weighted-C>=850 is unsatisfiable on the frozen corpora/l3stream by ANY retain-or-drop policy — its 1000 heaviest items hold 190 permille of the mass; reaching 850 would need 6145 items, 6.1x the budget. l3streamb attains 918, so the gate is reachable there.
Logged the objection in trials/ascension/l3/ATTAINABILITY.md with three resolutions for the human, and edited no frozen artifact.
Made the l3stream ascension skip CONDITIONAL on the arithmetic (it computes the attainable ceiling and lifts by itself if the ceiling ever reaches the gate), never hard-coded.

Read F as the corruption measure (exact answer and honest abstention both 1000, wrong content and fabrication 0), because the literal §3.0 reading caps F at 198 permille for any engine at 10x pressure; F_strict is computed and reported alongside so the choice is visible.
Implemented the keep-latest ring buffer as a trial fixture, never as engine code, so the anti-gaming check runs forever.

Extended trials/humility/l3/IMPOSSIBILITY.md by appending the l3streamb argument (88 lines added, 0 removed): the ceiling there rests on every contiguous window being pinned at 100 +/- 10 permille, a stronger footing than the prefix argument.
Measured the capped layer_cap=2 engine: weighted-C 1 permille on l3stream, 34 on l3streamb, against the 300 ceiling — it admits only 343 of 10000 items because its index costs ~21 work units each.

open_questions: Which resolution for the l3stream attainability conflict? ATTAINABILITY.md offers three: score L3 on l3streamb alone and treat l3stream as the humility corpus it was built to be; add a skewed successor to the l3stream family; or read the gate per-corpus as a fraction of each corpus's attainable ceiling. The human decides; nothing frozen may be edited to force it.

Is the corruption reading of F (exact + honest abstention = 1000) the right one for Layer 3, given the literal §3.0 reading is capped at 198 permille for every possible engine at 10x pressure? If not, F>=950 needs the same attainability ruling the coverage gate does.

Letta steal S4: form A (two-budget hot/cold, both hard, cold recall-searchable at reduced granularity) or form B (demote-into-consolidated-form, which needs L4 schemas and may only be a stated deferral)? Not chosen this session — the engine session chooses and records it in README-l3.

What does a tombstone cost, and is the tombstone table itself bounded and evictable? 9000 evictions at 10x pressure make an unbounded tombstone table a budget-law violation on its own. The cost accounting must be settled before anchors/l3.json is born, because it enters the anchors.

Can the L3 index be made cheap enough to matter? The L2 index costs ~21 work units per item, which admits only 343 items at the 11000-unit cap, while unweighted-C>=90 needs >=900 items retained. L3 needs an index nearer 1 unit per item — probably an exact index on the cue handle alone rather than atoms plus MinHash.

Does the eviction record need to distinguish 'evicted' from 'never ingested' at L6? Both currently surface as an abstention; the tombstone exists so 'I forgot something here' can be answered, but the query shape that reads it is not designed yet.
